chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَكَى بَعْضُ الثِّقَاتِ بِنَيْسَابُورَ: أَنَّهُ خَرَجَ لِإِسْحَاقَ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ مِنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ تَوْقِيعٌ: يَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنَ إِسْمَاعِيلَ … وَ يَا إِسْحَاقُ اقْرَأْ كِتَابَنَا عَلَى الْبِلَالِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ الثِّقَةُ الْمَأْمُونُ الْعَارِفُ بِمَا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ …

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: One of the Thiqat in Naysabur relayed to us that: There came out a signed rescript [Tawqi] from Abi Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Ishaq b. Ismail saying: O Ishaq b. Ismail … and O Ishaq – read this letter of ours to al-Bilali – may Allah be well pleased with him – for he is the Thiqa and the trusted one, the one who recognizes what is incumbent on him …

en.summary: This rescript (Tawqi) from Imam al-Hadi (peace be upon him) highlights the critical role of al-Bilali as a trusted intermediary in the Shia scholarly network, emphasizing his reliability (thiqa) and deep understanding of religious obligations. It reflects the historical practice of using authenticated deputies to transmit authoritative instructions during the period of the Minor and Major Occultations, ensuring doctrinal continuity.
en.seo_question: Who is al-Bilali and why is he considered trustworthy in Shia hadith literature?

key_terms.تَوْقِيع: Signed rescript or letter from the Imam
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be well pleased with him
